programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Scottish Women's Premier League (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: An dearbaidh Dhùn Èideann eadar Hearts agus Hibernian à Tynecastle beò air BBC ALBA. An geama slàn ri fhaicinn le aithris bho Donna NicNeill. The Edinburgh derby at Tynecastle as Hearts take on Hibernian live on BBC ALBA. Full match coverage with commentary from Donna MacNeill.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air bothan a dhèanamh anns an taigh agus a' faighinn tòrr spòrs bho bhith cluich anns an uisge. Tha facal an là-an-diugh co-cheangailte ri cumail tioram, cuideachd. Dè th'ann agus càite an lorg iad e? The Abadas have made a den inside the house and are having a lot of fun playing in the rain. Today's word has something to do with keeping dry, too. What could it be and where will they find it?

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Pompon 's a phàrantan ag ullachadh 'son turas air falbh, feumaidh Pompon tighinn gu co-dhùnadh air dè tha riatanach a thoirt leis sa bhaga aige. When Pompon and his parents prepare to go on a trip, Pompon must come to a decision as to what is essential for him to take in his bag.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha cuid dhe na rudan as fheàrr le Àtaidh agus Tilidh a dhìth. A bheil cuideigin air an goid? ’S e rùn-dìomhair a th’ ann! Some of Abney and Teal’s favourite objects are missing. Has there been a robbery? It’s a mystery!

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Tha Sionnach airson ’s gum bi co-là-breith sònraichte aig Maigheach. Tha cuireadh aig Comhachag is Tosg, fhad ’s a bheir iad prèasant brèagha thuice, leithid dìthean le fàileadh cùbhraidh. Chan eil sin cho furasta ’s a shaoileas iad. Fhad ’s a tha iad trang a’ lorg nam prèasantan tha Maigheach air bhioran ’s I a’ feitheamh gus an tòisich am pàrtaidh co-là-breith aice. Fox wants to give Hare the best birthday ever. Owl and Tusk are invited, but only if they bring a nice present, like a beautifully scented flower. But that is not quite as easy as it seems. All the while Hare is kept waiting for her birthday party to start.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: SPFL
programme.desc: Ball-coise bho Lìog a h-Aon le Hamilton Academical a’ cur fàilte air Ross County, beò air BBC ALBA. An geama beò ri fhaicinn le preasantair Alasdair MacIllinnein agus aithris bho Ailig O’Henley. Join BBC Alba for live League 1 football action as Hamilton Academical host Ross County. Full coverage with presenter Alasdair MacLennan and commentary from Alex O’Henley.

programme.title: Rurachd (Foraging)
programme.desc: Mary Ann Kennedy and Lucy Cooke: a foraged feast with musical friends in Galloway. Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Liusaidh Cooke le stòras nàdair. Ròic na Rùrachd le càirdean ciùil an Gall Ghàidhealaibh.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Rathad Ramsay
programme.desc: Ramsay meets Kim Carnie on the island of Kerrera, where they walk along picturesque bays with panoramic views of Oban Bay and the Slate Islands. Kim discusses the importance of Gaelic in her life and how that has shaped her career as a singer. She opens up about love and identity, and how that has evolved over the years, whilst enjoying the surrounding nature and fresh autumn air. San treas sreath de Rathad Ramsay bidh Ramsay MacMahon a’ coinneachadh ri sàr Ghàidheil bho air feadh Alba ‘s iad a’ co-roinn sgeulachdan, cuir luach air nàdar agus a’ cnuasachadh ma beatha. Tha Ramsay a’ coinneachadh ri Kim Carnie air eilean Chearrara far a bheil iad air an cuartachadh le bàghean àlainn agus seallaidhean air leth den Òban agus na h-Eileanan Sglèata. Innsidh Kim cho cudromach ‘s a tha Gàidhlig na beatha ‘s a bhuaidh a tha seo air a thoirt air a beatha agus air a dreuchd na seinneadair. Gu follaiseach dèidheil air àm an fhoghair agus an àrainneachd ghlan mun cuairt, tha i fuasgladh suas ma beachdan air gaol, fèin-aithne agus mar a tha sin air obrachadh a-mach na beatha fhèin. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. A’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Talisk, Julie Fowlis/Éamon Doorley/Zoë Conway/John Mc Intyre, Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols agus Pine Tree Flyers. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Talisk; Julie Fowlis, Éamon Doorley, Zoë Conway, John McIntyre; Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols and Pine Tree Flyers. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ro Thrath don t-Saoghal/Born too Soon
programme.desc: Obair sgioba an Aonad Dlùth-chùram Leanabain ’s iad a’ coimhead an dèidh naoidheanan so-leònta. The work of the NICU team and their care for vulnerable babies.

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Thàinig an ola gu Fraochy Bay ach de a' bhuaidh a tha e air a thoirt air a' bhaile agus na daoine? Agus de cho fada sa sheasas e, agus de ni muinntir a' bhaile leis an dìleab? Fraochy Bay has experienced an oil boom, but just as quickly as it arrived it dries up, causing a swift departure of the oil industry. How will the townsfolk deal with the leftovers?

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: An greimean lòin as fheàrr le Abigail, 's e Buntàta Cruasbach Sàiste. 'Ad cho blast' 's a tha 'ad rin ithe. Tha 'n seòrs' aice-se soirbh a dhèanamh; feumaidh tu fheuchainn. Abigail’s favourite snack lunch is crispy sage potatoes. It's as nice to look at as to eat and her version is easy to make - you must try it! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Steelmen
programme.desc: Ann an 1991, bha baile Thobar na Màthar a’ greimeachadh ris a’ bhuaidh shòisealta, eaconamach agus chultarail a bheireadh dùnadh ionad stàilinn Ravenscraig air an sgìre, ach airson a’ chiad uair ann an 39 bliadhna thog sgioba ball-coise a’ bhaile, na ‘Steelmen' mar a theirear riutha, Cupa na h-Alba, a’ toirt boillsgeadh dòchais a thogadh an dorchadas. In 1991, as the town of Motherwell faced the crippling social, economic and cultural impact of the closure of the Ravenscraig steelworks, its football club, locally known as the Steelmen, lifted the prestigious Scottish Cup for the first time in 39 years. The victory was a glimmer of light in the ensuing darkness.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Fiona NicChoinnich agus Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilte air luchd-amhairc chun a’ chuid às fheàrr de Fhèis Belladrum 2022. Anns a' phrògram seo, cothrom am prìomh thaisbeanadh air Àrd-ùrlar a Ghàrraidh bho oidhche Dhiardaoin na Fèise fhaicinn. Bha an t-àite loma-làn airson an taisbeanadh aig an t-seinneadair chliùiteach Emile Sandé, a tha air soirbheachadh mu mòr mar sgrìobhaiche òran agus air na milleanan de chlàran album a reic air feadh an t-saoghail. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain MacDonald host highlights from the Belladrum festival, 2022. This programme features the headlining act from the Garden Stage on Thursday night at the festival. Performing in front of a packed audience was acclaimed singer Emeli Sandé, one of Britain’s most successful songwriters, having sold millions of albums worldwide.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc: Skipinnish le Last of the Hunters ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann. Skipinnish perform Last of the Hunters in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Le cuideachadh bho Burtaidh, tha Sif a’ toirt Pipp agus Bran air dàn-chuairt fèill spòrs. Ziff leads Pipp and Button on a fairground adventure with help from faithful Bertie.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ mì-thoilichte oir chan fhaod e cluich leis an spàin bhrot’ oir tha ro mhòr dha. Gu fortanach, tha Beag a’ moladh gum faod e taic a thoirt dhaibh-san le bhith toirt am brot air ais dhan uamh – is abair g’eil e taiceil! Baby Soup Dragon is unhappy - he isn’t allowed to play with the soup spoon as it’s too big for him. Fortunately, Small suggests that he can help to deliver the soup instead - and he is hugely helpful!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha bogsa dìomhaireachd air laighe air a’ phlanaid, le rudan annasach na bhroinn - clobhdan a tha nan tuill cuideachd. Tha e comasach dha na Clangairean siubhal tro na tuill seo - agus abair gu bheil iad trang a’ siubhal! A mysterious box has landed on the planet, with curious things inside it - cloths which are also holes. The Clangers can travel through these holes, and they do it a lot!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha a’ ghrian a’ deàrrsadh ‘s tha Ooona'son dhol a dh’iasgach. Tha May ag aontachadh cluich cuide ri Baba ach tha Baba a’ diùltadh faiche nan gràineag fhàgail gus an dùisg Spiky bho chadal-geamhraidh! It’s a beautiful day and Oona wants to practise fishing. May offers to play with Baba, who refuses to leave the hedgehog burrow as he wants to wait until Spiky wakes from his hibernation!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona daonnan ann an cabhag ach tha Papa airson sealltainn dhi gum bi buthaidean a' gabhail cùisean air an socair. Saoil an tig aice air ionnsachadh rudan a dhèanamh ann an ‘Dòigh na Buthaide? Oona is forever in a hurry to learn and get things done, but Papa wants to show her that puffins tend to approach things in a slow and steady fashion. Will Oona master the ‘Way of the Puffin?’

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Sula a’ tadhal air Bing ‘s i air a h-aodann a pheantadh mar dhealan-dè, tha i airson aodann Bing a’ pheantadh cuideachd. Chaneil am peantadh a' dol ro mhath ach tha e sealbhach gu bheil Flop ri làimh airson gnothaichean a rèiteachadh. When Sula visits Bing with her face painted like a butterfly, she also wants to face paint Bing. But the painting doesn’t go well for them. Fortunately, Flop is on hand to sort it all out.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Tha Bing brònach nuair a thèid innse dha, an-dèidh dha a’ bhanachdach fhaighinn, nach eil gin de na steigearan sònraichte as fheàrr leis air fhàgail. Tha cùisean ag atharrachadh ge-tà nuair a tha e a’ faighinn teisteanas grinn, sònraichte. Bing is sad when he is told, after having had his vaccination, that there are none of his favourite stickers left at Dr Molly’s surgery. He soon cheers up though when he is given a very special certificate instead.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Tha tòrr spòrs aig Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur an ìre gur e ròbotan a th’ annta, gus am brùth cuideigin aca putan is tha an aileag a’ tòiseachadh air Peicein. Carson nach stad an aileag aige? Bheil smachd aig cuideigin air à àiteigin eile? Chan urrainn do Ghriogair sguir a shreothartaich, Lòra a mhèaranaich neo Raghnall a chasadaich. Saoil a bheil iad uile a’ tionndadh nan ròbotan dhà-rìribh? Petit and his friends are having a lot of fun pretending to be robots, until one of them presses a button and Petit gets the hiccups. Why can't he stop hiccupping? Is someone else controlling him from somewhere? Greg can't stop sneezing, Laura yawns and Roman coughs. Could it be that everyone is turning into real life robots?

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Tha Hilda a’ tionndadh gu leabhar dìomhair airson ionnsachadh mar a chuidicheas i beathannan Dhaibhidh agus a màthair – ach, mo chreach, abair gu ‘eil a coibhneis cosgail is croiseil dhaibh uile. Hilda turns to a mysterious book to learn how she can better the lives of Daibhidh and her mother, but being kind proves to be costly and problematic for all.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Nuair tha Greta an cù a’ cèilidh air an sgoil, tha Flix airson a bhith taiceil dhi. Gu mì-fhortanach tha iad glè mhì-mhodhail nuair a tha ‘ad còmhla. Tha seo ag adhbharachadh trioblaid coin-cait ach the feum air fuasgladh cait-coin. When Greta the dog visits the school, Flix wants to be helpful to her. Unfortunately, they’re very badly behaved when together. This causes a dog-cat problem so what’s needed is a cat-dog solution!

programme.title: Geamaichean Gorach
programme.desc: Tha cùisean a-dol ceàrr leis na Farpaisich ach tha a’ Chrùbag faisg air làimh le cobhair, tòrr ruitheam agus an 'cha cha cha'! Things go awry with the competitors, but Crùbag is near to hand, with lots of rhythm and the 'cha cha cha'!

programme.title: A-null ’s a-nall
programme.desc: Tha Isra cho toilichte nuair a tha i a’ faighinn an cothrom càmpadh mar a sìnnsearan - na Bedouin - còmhla ri a caraid, Laoise. Isra is delighted when she gets the chance to go camping like her ancestors, the Bedouin, with her friend, Laoise.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Seachd Là
programme.desc: Local, national and international news from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Ann am prògram às an tasglann bho 2009, Salm 31 air a sheinn le Ceathrar-cheòil Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìleach Ghlaschu, Laoidh Chalum Chille le Còisir Ghàidhlig Bhaile Ghobhainn agus bidh Torcuil MacLeòid ag innse mun phàirt a th' aig creideamh na bheatha fhèin. Air aithris le Iain MacFhionghain. In an archival edition from 2009, Psalm 31 sung by the Glasgow Islay Gaelic Choir Quartet, the hymn Laoidh Chalum Chille by Govan Gaelic Choir, and Torquil MacLeod tells his personal faith story. Presented by Iain MacKinnon. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Cidsin Granaidh Chalanais
programme.desc: Gregor makes his grannie’s gingerbread and classic Scottish tablet, and adds his own flair to her fishcake recipe.

programme.title: Rùm Gu Rùm, Le Erica
programme.desc: Actress turned interior designer, Erica Macpherson, takes us on a design adventure throughout the Highlands and Islands. With the help of local craft workers she finds new ideas for designing old spaces. Tha an cleasaiche, a tha a-nis na dealbhaiche cruthachail thaighean, Erica Nic a’ Phersain, a’ gabhail sgrìob tron Ghàidhealtachd ‘s na h-Eileanan. Le taic bho luchd-ciùird, tha i a’ lorg dhòighean ùra air seann rumanan a thoirt beò. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Surfing: Marcachd an Tuinn/Riding the Wave
programme.desc: Tha Ceitlin Lilidh a’ toirt thugainn sreath de dhà phàirt air eachdraidh surfadh air feadh an t-saoghail. Ceitlin Lilidh's series on the world history of surfing.

programme.title: Seirm
programme.desc: Prògram de cheòl traidiseanta agus freumhach air a lìbhrigeadh le Màiri Anna NicUalraig. A’ taisbeanaidh chlàraidhean is chòmhraidhean a chaidh a dhèanamh aig àm Celtic Connections 2024, chìte cuid den luchd-ciùil a b’ fheàrr a bha aig an fhèis, leithid Talisk, Julie Fowlis/Éamon Doorley/Zoë Conway/John Mc Intyre, Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols agus Pine Tree Flyers. Traditional and roots music show presented by Mary Ann Kennedy. Filmed during Celtic Connections 2024, Seirm showcases bespoke recordings and conversations with some of the best artists appearing at the festival. This episode features performances from Talisk; Julie Fowlis, Éamon Doorley, Zoë Conway, John McIntyre; Glen Hansard & Breanndán Ó Beaglaoich, Buffalo Nichols and Pine Tree Flyers. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: We explore the surprising ways animals use touch to sense their world, find food and stay out of danger.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: An greimean lòin as fheàrr le Abigail, 's e Buntàta Cruasbach Sàiste. 'Ad cho blast' 's a tha 'ad rin ithe. Tha 'n seòrs' aice-se soirbh a dhèanamh; feumaidh tu fheuchainn. Abigail’s favourite snack lunch is crispy sage potatoes. It's as nice to look at as to eat and her version is easy to make - you must try it! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: Tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean air an dòigh glan nuair tha na duilleagan a’ cuachail gu talamh! Daolag-bhreac and Seillean are delighted when the leaves start twirling to the ground!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha seillean glacte ann an uamhag Bhernie agus, gun e air biadh fhaighinn, tha e cho fann ‘s nach dèan e a shlighe dhachaigh! Ge-tà, tha Oona ‘s Baba deònach a dhol a-lorg biadh dha gus am fàs e làidir a-rithist! There’s a bee trapped in Bernie’s grotto but without anything to eat, he has become too weak to escape and make his way back to the hive. However, Oona and Baba are on hand to find and bring him the food he needs to build his strength back up!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Mossy airson a dhol air turas-ionmhais bidhe ach ‘s ann a dh’ fheumas an sgioba dhol air misean-seilg' eadar-dhealaichte 's Pip ‘s Pop air a dhol am falach air Otto bochd! Mossy wants the gang to join him on a food hunt, but they are all called on a different sort of search when Pip and Pop decide to hide on poor Otto!

programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Nuair tha ruitheam a’ chiùil bhon rèidio a’ còrdadh ri Boban cho mòr ‘s gu bheil e toirt air danns', chan eil Fuigheag buileach a' tuigs' na gluasadan bodhaig a tha seo! Boban enjoys the rhythm of the music on the radio so much, that he begins to dance. But Fuigheag isn’t sure what these movements are all about!

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Tha Sif, Pipp agus Bran a’ gabhail pàirt ann an latha chleasan nan Losgann. Ziff, Pipp and Button compete in their own Froggie sports day.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Gach oidhche bidh Comhachag a’ cumail geàrd air a’ choille. Ge-tà, leis a’ ghealach a’ sìor fhàs tana agus a’ choille a’ sìor fhàs dorcha, tha Comhachag a’ fàs aonranach. Chan eil e idir cho measail air a dhleastanas. Gu fortanach, tha plàna aig Maigheach! Every night, Owl keeps watch over the forest. But with the Moon growing thinner and the woods growing darker night by night, Owl begins to feel lonely. He starts to dread his duties. Luckily, Hare has a plan!

programme.title: Pompon Am Mathan Beag/Pompon Little Bear
programme.desc: Tha Mamaidh air rud dìomhair innse do Phompon - tha i air cuirm a' chur air dòigh 'son cò-là-breith Dadaidh - ach ciamar a chumas Pompon an rùn-dìomhair? Mamaidh has told Pompon a secret - she's arranged a party for Daddy's birthday. But how will Pompon keep the secret?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Gilleasbaig Fearghasdan a’ leughadh Mèirleach nan Dathan. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Gabriel Alborozo, agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Gilleasbaig Ferguson reads Mèirleach nan Dathan, written and illustrated by Gabriel Alborozo and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: SpongeBob
programme.desc: Man Ray rents Squidward's house. Tha An Sòrnan a’ gabhail taigh Ghiobaird air mhàl.

programme.title: An Sgoil
programme.desc: Leis mar a chaidh sgrùdadh na sgoile an-uiridh, tha bòrd na sgoile air Leas-Cheannard ùr, Ms Dallas, a thoirt a-steach gus sùil ghèir a chumail air Mgr Mackle. Bidh sinn a' coinneachadh ri tidsearean ùra agus ri feadhainn air a bheil sinn air eòlas a chuir roimhe. After last year’s school inspection, the school board has appointed a new deputy head, Ms Dallas, to keep an eye on Mr Mackle. We meet new teachers alongside some recognisable personalities.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc: Tha eadar-dhealaichidhean air an comharrachadh san sgoil is, mar dhùbhlain, tha aig Flix is Burma ri bhith càirdeil ri chèile. Chan eil fhios ciamar a dh'obraicheas seo a-mach ge-tà! Differences are celebrated in school and, as a challenge, Flix and Burma have to be friendly with one another. Nobody knows how this will work out though!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Nuair tha Bonns is Uilidh a' sàbhaladh Throig bhon Bhògais-shìd’, tha e uabhasach neo-thaingeil. Cho neo-thaingeil ‘s gu bheil e a' tilleadh air ais chun na Bògaisean. Ach tha e ag ionnsachadh gu bheil caraidean feumail aig a' cheann thall! When Bonns and Uilidh save Troig from Bògais-shìd’, he is very ungrateful. So much so, that he returns to see the Bògaisean. However, he learns that friends are helpful, at the end of the day!

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Uilidh airson dearbhadh gu bheil e treun – dìreach mar an Gumbal gun Ainm. Ciamar a thèid dha? Bheil e treun no bheil e dìreach gòrach? Uilidh wants to prove that he is a hero just like the Un-named Gumbal. How will he get on? Is he brave or is he just foolish?

programme.title: Fillte
programme.desc: Fillte goes on a journey throughout Scotland to discover the history and contemporary hand-crafted practice behind the artisan production of woven fabrics, such as wool, hemp, linen, grasses, leather and many more unorthodox materials. Tha Fillte a gabhail turas tro Alba a’ sireadh eachdraidh agus sgeulachdan an latha ’n diugh co-cheangailte ris an luchd-ciùird a tha snìomh ‘s ag obrachadh diofar stuthan, leithid, clòimh, corcach, anart, feur,leathar, agus iomadh seorsa stuth iongantach eile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean visits Airth in Stirlingshire where he discovers a fruity architectural surprise.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Seo an fharpais-cheist far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Le Niall Iain Dòmnhallach aig an stiùir cluichidh na sgiobaidhean anns an stiùideo an aghaidh an ochdnar Mas Fhìoraich a tha a’ cluich bhon dachaighean fhèin agus a tha a’ cur nan ceistean. A’ strì an aghaidh na Mas Fhìoraich airson feuchainn air an duais mhòr, tha DK is Kenna agus Kirsty is Seònaid. Presented by Niall Iain MacDonald, this is the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Playing from the comfort of their own homes are the Pretenders, and they are the ones posing the questions. Battling the Pretenders to win the big prize are DK and Kenna, and Kirsty and Janet. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Trusadh
programme.desc: Ciamar a tha fuil-mìos a’ toirt buaidh air boireannaich? How do periods affect women?

programme.title: An Clo Mor
programme.desc: After years of unhappiness, mill worker Mairead finally walks out of her decades-long marriage and into the arms of the person she loves - hotel owner Cairistiona. However, as the women agree to wait for the right time to tell Mairead’s husband Boyd they are together, little do they know there’s someone watching from the shadows. Às dèidh bliadhnaichean de mhì-thoileachas, tha neach-obrach na muilne, Mairead, a’ fàgail an duine aice às dèidh bliadhnaichean fada pòsta airson a bhith còmhla ris an neach air a bheil gaol aice – Cairistìona, aig a bheil an taigh-òsta. Ach, ged a tha na boireannaich agaontachadh feitheamh gus innse dha Boyd, an duine aig Mairead, gu bheil iad còmhla – ‘s beag a dh’fhios a th’ aca gu bheil cuideigin ‘san dorchadas gan coimhead. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Am Balla (The Wall)
programme.desc: Tha Ramsay MacMahon a’ dol air turas gus ionnsachadh mun sgaradh mòr eadar beartas agus bochdainn ann an São Paulo, Braisil. Bho na coimhearsnachdan beartach glaiste air cùl gheataichean tèarainteachd gu na favelas a tha a’ cuir thairis le sluagh, tha ballachan do-fhaicsinneach a’ sgaradh dhaoine bho chèile sa bhaile seo. Air an turas aige, cluinnidh Ramsay bho dhaoine a tha feuchainn ris an sgaradh seo a thoirt às a chèile le bhith a’ cruthachadh chothroman do dhaoine ann an cuid de na coimhearsnachdan far a bheil an ana-chothrom as motha ri fhaicinn. Ramsay MacMahon goes on a journey to find out about the deep divide between wealth and poverty in São Paulo, Brazil. From the affluent gated communities to the overcrowded favelas, invisible walls separate people in this city. On his journey, Ramsay hears from individuals who are determined to break down division by creating opportunities for people within some of the city's most disadvantaged communities. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Faodail
programme.desc: Tha Tasglann Fhilm Faodail a’ tarraing aire gu filmichean dhùthchasach Innse Gall bho na 1930an gu na 80an, a bha caillte ach a-nis glèidhte don ghinealach ri teachd. Tha bhana Cinema Sgìre Leantainneach a’ siubhal nan eilean, a’ taisbeanadh fhilmichean sna sgìrean ionadail, le cothrom am faicinn air-loidhne air feadh an t-saoghail. Cuirear aithris bheairteach ùr riutha, a’ buntainn ris a’ Ghàidhealtachd, airson luchd-amhairc an là an-diugh. The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s-1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgìre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gàidhealtachd for contemporary audiences. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Glan Fhèin
programme.desc: A mockumentary shadowing a company that services short-term lets. Angela and Katie aim to clean up and give the competition a bleaching. Blockages need to be dealt with, not just unclogging hot tub filters. A new staff member has a few skeletons in his cupboard but ex-con Daniel hopes he has a squeaky-clean future. Meanwhile, Betty meets Daniel’s pregnant partner Dido and checks in on her beloved pet pooch Buster. Soon the police are knocking on the company’s Portakabin door. Written by and starring Hannah McKirdy and Lana Pheutan.

programme.title: Girls in Bands at the BBC
programme.desc: Compilation celebrating some guitar band performances at the BBC that feature some of the best female musicians in rock. Beginning with the oft-forgotten American group Fanny performing You're the One, it's a journey along rock's spectrum from the 1970s to now. The selection includes the powerful vocals of Elkie Brooks on Vinegar Joe's Proud to Be a Honky Woman, the mesmerising poetry of Patti Smith's Horses and the upbeat energy of The Go-Go's on We Got the Beat. Mighty basslines come courtesy of Tina Weymouth on Psycho Killer and Kim Gordon on Sugar Kane, whilst we trace the line of indie rock from the Au Pairs through Lush, Elastica and Garbage to current band Savages.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: Bruno Brookes and Sybil Ruscoe present the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 10 November 1988 and featuring Brother Beyond, Bryan Ferry, Robin Beck, Salt-N-Pepa, INXS, Chris de Burgh, Deacon Blue, Enya and Prince.

programme.desc: David Jensen presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 11 November 1982. Featuring Blue Zoo, A Flock of Seagulls, Clannad, Dionne Warwick, Donna Summer, Marvin Gaye, Eddy Grant and Zoo.

programme.desc: Tony Blackburn presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 23 September 1976 and featuring Smokie, Kiki Dee, The Drifters, Manfred Mann's Earth Band, The Wurzels, Bay City Rollers, Rod Stewart, ABBA, and dance sequences from Ruby Flipper.

programme.desc: Richard Blackwood presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 4 August 2000 and featuring Macy Gray, Bomfunk MCs, Santana, Samantha Mumba, Point Break, Moloko, Janet Jackson and Craig David.

programme.desc: Jayne Middlemiss presents the pop chart programme, first broadcast on 11 August 2000 and featuring Craig David, Reef, Wookie & Lain, Mansun, Storm, MJ Cole, Ronan Keating and Robbie Williams.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: Documentary presenting an intimate portrait of one of Britain's most charming wild animals, following a family of water voles living on a canal in Derbyshire though a typical year. The picturesque Cromford canal used to serve the region's cotton mills. Now, having been deserted, it serves as a perfect water vole paradise. For these hyperactive little mammals, a year is nearly a lifetime. They spend their lives in a frenzy of activity - swimming, feeding and breeding - the latter of most necessity, since water voles are becoming a rarity.

programme.title: Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: Michael Palin circles the Pacific Rim through 18 countries. After a journey on a rusty ferry through the dangerous Sulu Sea, he arrives in Borneo at monsoon time. From the rainforest, he heads off to the long houses of the Iban tribesmen and the secret heart of Borneo. Across the equator in Java, the most densely populated island in the world, he visits the largest monument in the southern hemisphere.

programme.title: Miss Marple
programme.desc: In the late 1940s, Gerry Burton, accompanied by his sister Joanna, goes to the little village of Lymston to convalesce after an accident. The village seems to welcome them with open arms. But there are dark mysterious undercurrents at work and it's not long before Miss Marple comes to visit.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Treasures
programme.desc: Dan is captivated by the sword of a Samurai warrior and the artistry employed to make this beautiful instrument of death. By contrast, he finds solace and tranquillity in a Japanese temple and meditation garden.

programme.title: Ran
programme.desc: Akira Kurosawa's epic masterpiece is a reworking of Shakespeare's King Lear set in medieval Japan. After a lifetime of battles, 70-year-old Lord Hidetora announces that he is passing his authority to his eldest son Taro. The youngest son Saburo protests and is banished from the kingdom. But instead of fulfilling their father's wishes, Taro and middle brother Jiro are disloyal to the former lord and attack his castle. Hidetora survives but following his sons' betrayal is now losing his mind. When Jiro has his brother murdered, the banished Saburo and his allies return to fight a battle against the remaining brother. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Sam Shepard narrates a documentary profile of celebrated Japanese film-maker Akira Kurosawa, responsible for the films Seven Samurai, Ikiru and Rashomon.

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Stately sitcom. A repair bill for Audrey's Rolls-Royce finally convinces her to revert to four-legged horsepower.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Sitcom. When Hyacinth hears that Emmet is rehearsing a musical, she is beside herself. Unfortunately sorting out Daddy's antics has to take priority.

programme.title: People's Palaces: The Golden Age of Civic Architecture
programme.desc: Jonathan Foyle explores some of the best Georgian and Victorian neo-classical civic buildings across the north of England in a story of rivalry, ambition and power.

programme.title: The Medici: Makers of Modern Art
programme.desc: Documentary in which Andrew Graham-Dixon reveals how the Medici family transformed Florence through sculpture, painting and architecture, and created a world where masterpieces fetch millions today. Without the money and patronage of the Medici we might never have heard of artists such as Donatello, Michelangelo or Botticelli. Graham-Dixon examines how a family of shadowy, corrupt businessmen, driven by greed and ambition, became the financial engine behind the Italian Renaissance.

programme.title: Britain's Most Fragile Treasure
programme.desc: Dr Janina Ramirez unlocks the secrets of a centuries-old masterpiece in glass, the Great East Window at York Minster, the largest expanse of medieval stained glass in the UK.

programme.title: Gilbert and Sullivan’s The Gondoliers
programme.desc: Scottish Opera's sparkling staging of Gilbert and Sullivan's witty satire. Audiences are transported to Venice for a joyful production packed with some of the pair's most-loved songs.

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom
programme.desc: Three-part series that looks at a year in Alaska, revealing the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush.

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: Artist Lachlan Goudie explores how, at the turn of the 19th century, Scotland's artists challenged the traditions they had inherited and, embracing new ways of seeing and painting from the Continent, revolutionised Scottish art. From the Glasgow Boys' intimate rural realism, to Arthur Melville's brilliantly experimental watercolours; from Hill House, Charles Rennie Mackintosh's 'total work of art', to JD Fergusson's pioneering Scottish modernism, this generation transformed the way we saw Scotland's landscape and identity.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Salford University. The specialist subjects are British politics 1900-1918, the operas of Gilbert and Sullivan, the Indian tribes of North America 1550-1900 and the political history of China since 1911.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Marshall are joined by guest panellists Gemma Craven, Leslie Thomas, Kate O'Mara and Brian Blessed.

programme.title: This Cultural Life
programme.desc: Singer-songwriter and composer Rufus Wainwright talks to John Wilson about his creative influences.

programme.title: Three's Company
programme.desc: Mary Marquis in conversation with poets Douglas Dunn and Craig Raine.

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: In a story where progress meets invention, this film looks at how the blacksmith created items in wrought and cast iron that both served and embellished society. From the earliest ornate hinges and doors to magnificent baroque gates and mass-produced street furniture, it reveals the mastery of metalworkers. They include Jean Tijou, Robert Bakewell and John Tresilian, the designs of Robert Adam and George Gilbert Scott, and the mass marketers of the Victorian age such as the Saracen foundry. Treasures are drawn from all corners of the UK in a celebration of the best of British decorative ironwork.

Across the equator in Java, the most densely populated island in the world, he visits the largest monument in the southern hemisphere.

programme.title: Miss Marple
programme.desc: In the late 1940s, Gerry Burton, accompanied by his sister Joanna, goes to the little village of Lymston to convalesce after an accident. The village seems to welcome them with open arms. But there are dark mysterious undercurrents at work and it's not long before Miss Marple comes to visit.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Treasures
programme.desc: Dan is captivated by the sword of a Samurai warrior and the artistry employed to make this beautiful instrument of death. By contrast, he finds solace and tranquillity in a Japanese temple and meditation garden.

programme.title: Ran
programme.desc: Akira Kurosawa's epic masterpiece is a reworking of Shakespeare's King Lear set in medieval Japan. After a lifetime of battles, 70-year-old Lord Hidetora announces that he is passing his authority to his eldest son Taro. The youngest son Saburo protests and is banished from the kingdom. But instead of fulfilling their father's wishes, Taro and middle brother Jiro are disloyal to the former lord and attack his castle. Hidetora survives but following his sons' betrayal is now losing his mind. When Jiro has his brother murdered, the banished Saburo and his allies return to fight a battle against the remaining brother. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Sam Shepard narrates a documentary profile of celebrated Japanese film-maker Akira Kurosawa, responsible for the films Seven Samurai, Ikiru and Rashomon.

programme.title: To the Manor Born

programme.title: The Medici: Makers of Modern Art
programme.desc: Documentary in which Andrew Graham-Dixon reveals how the Medici family transformed Florence through sculpture, painting and architecture, and created a world where masterpieces fetch millions today. Without the money and patronage of the Medici we might never have heard of artists such as Donatello, Michelangelo or Botticelli. Graham-Dixon examines how a family of shadowy, corrupt businessmen, driven by greed and ambition, became the financial engine behind the Italian Renaissance.

programme.desc: Three-part series that looks at a year in Alaska, revealing the stories of pioneering Alaskans, both animal and human, as they battle the elements and reap the benefits of nature's seasonal gold rush.

programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: Artist Lachlan Goudie explores how, at the turn of the 19th century, Scotland's artists challenged the traditions they had inherited and, embracing new ways of seeing and painting from the Continent, revolutionised Scottish art. From the Glasgow Boys' intimate rural realism, to Arthur Melville's brilliantly experimental watercolours; from Hill House, Charles Rennie Mackintosh's 'total work of art', to JD Fergusson's pioneering Scottish modernism, this generation transformed the way we saw Scotland's landscape and identity.

programme.title: Classic Mastermind
programme.desc: Magnus Magnusson presents the quiz programme from Salford University. The specialist subjects are British politics 1900-1918, the operas of Gilbert and Sullivan, the Indian tribes of North America 1550-1900 and the political history of China since 1911.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Marshall are joined by guest panellists Gemma Craven, Leslie Thomas, Kate O'Mara and Brian Blessed.

programme.title: This Cultural Life

programme.title: Three's Company
programme.desc: Mary Marquis in conversation with poets Douglas Dunn and Craig Raine.

programme.title: Metalworks!
programme.desc: In a story where progress meets invention, this film looks at how the blacksmith created items in wrought and cast iron that both served and embellished society. From the earliest ornate hinges and doors to magnificent baroque gates and mass-produced street furniture, it reveals the mastery of metalworkers. They include Jean Tijou, Robert Bakewell and John Tresilian, the designs of Robert Adam and George Gilbert Scott, and the mass marketers of the Victorian age such as the Saracen foundry. Treasures are drawn from all corners of the UK in a celebration of the best of British decorative ironwork.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: It's been a week of great consequence for the media. On Monday, Russell Brand was sentenced to over ten years in prison for rape and sexual assault. On Tuesday - in a separate story - ITV News and The Guardian named David Walliams as the celebrity who tried to use an injunction to block the publication of sexual misconduct allegations. Our panel discusses the issues raised: Rosamund Urwin, chief news correspondent at The Sunday Times; Alex Wilson, partner at RPC, and Sarah Ditum, author of Toxic: Women, Fame and The Noughties.

programme.desc: South London zoologist and urban wildlife enthusiast, Lira Valencia, heads to Brazil to discover how humans and animals coexist in the most biodiverse country on earth. Lira begins her journey in the megacity of São Paulo, where she meets the people keeping the city's spectacular fauna safe from the expanding urban environment. She comes face to face with the cuddly, but powerful capybaras in São Paulo's public parks, and meets the puma family who've become stars in the local community.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: The AI industry has just had the fright of its life. After a shock US midterm election result handed Democrats control of both houses of Congress, the companies leading the AI revolution suddenly face an uncomfortable reality: investigations, subpoenas, public backlash and the prospect of sweeping new regulation. At the very centre of the storm is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, whose company sits at the heart of the global AI boom. Recent revelations surrounding Huang have triggered a crisis of confidence, wiped hundreds of billions from Nvidia's market value, and raised difficult questions about corporate governance, national security and the concentration of power inside the AI industry. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's political gamble appears to have backfired spectacularly. After pouring hundreds of millions of dollars into the midterms, Silicon Valley's most influential figures are now confronting a Congress that may be far less willing to give them the benefit of the doubt.

programme.title: The Interface
programme.desc: The show that reaches through your screen, to tell you the tech stories that ready matter. Hosted by BBC technology journalist Thomas Germain and social media expert Professor Jessica Maddox, The Interface dives into the stories, trends, apps, gadgets, algorithms and internet obsessions shaping how we live, work, think and connect. From AI and influencers to memes, data leaks, cybersecurity and the weirdest corners of the web, The Interface explores what happens when technology collides with real life. Cutting through the hype, the hosts unpack the platforms, products and online phenomena that increasingly shape our choices, our culture and our sense of self - whether we like it or not! Sharp, insightful and often very funny, The Interface examines our relationship with technology in all its messy, brilliant, absurd and world-changing glory. Along the way, it tackles one of the biggest questions of our age: what kind of future are the likes of Elon Musk, Chat GPT and all the other Silicon Valley giants building, and does anyone really want to live there?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. A motorist races past traffic on an M53 slip road, while a bus squeezes past cyclists with barely room to spare, almost crushing them under the wheels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Honey

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: The results are in, and with a place in Blackpool at stake, the tension is high. The pros take on one of the biggest trends in fiction as they bring the world of romantasy to life for their latest group performance, and fresh from his victorious stint on The Celebrity Traitors, Bash Croft performs in the ballroom. Two couples will go head to head in the dance-off, but who will secure the final spot in the Tower Ballroom?

programme.desc: From winter storms to scorching summers, seasonal seas push animals to be resourceful, adaptable and adventurous. Those who can survive these dynamic seas reap rich rewards.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. A motorist races past traffic on an M53 slip road, while a bus squeezes past cyclists with barely room to spare, almost crushing them under the wheels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives

programme.title: Escape to the Country
