programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: The results are in, and with a place in Blackpool at stake, the tension is high. The pros take on one of the biggest trends in fiction as they bring the world of romantasy to life for their latest group performance, and fresh from his victorious stint on The Celebrity Traitors, Bash Croft performs in the ballroom. Two couples will go head to head in the dance-off, but who will secure the final spot in the Tower Ballroom?

programme.title: Blue Planet III

programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. A motorist races past traffic on an M53 slip road, while a bus squeezes past cyclists with barely room to spare, almost crushing them under the wheels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

programme.title: Honey

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek the weatherman reflects on some of his favourite walks from south Wales. In the Vale of Glamorgan, Derek is joined by Olympian Colin Jackson, and together they explore a five-mile coastal route that has it all - dinosaur footprints, World War II gun battery remains, the site of a major communication breakthrough and an iconic Victorian pier. In his second hand-picked wander, Derek walks from Port Talbot to Swansea and discovers a route full of contrasts. Amongst the heavy industrial landscape lie some surprising pockets of nature and a bustling marina. Derek also tries his hand at the helm of a luxury boat and narrowly avoids crashing into the harbour wall. Finally, Derek revisits Usk, where he comes across something unexpected - an airfield, home of the South Wales Gliding Club, which has been in operation for 60 years. Derek joins them for a weather briefing before taking to the skies himself, where he witnesses amazing views of Usk and the Bristol Channel.

programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road

The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek the weatherman reflects on some of his favourite walks from south Wales. In the Vale of Glamorgan, Derek is joined by Olympian Colin Jackson, and together they explore a five-mile coastal route that has it all - dinosaur footprints, World War II gun battery remains, the site of a major communication breakthrough and an iconic Victorian pier. In his second hand-picked wander, Derek walks from Port Talbot to Swansea and discovers a route full of contrasts. Amongst the heavy industrial landscape lie some surprising pockets of nature and a bustling marina. Derek also tries his hand at the helm of a luxury boat and narrowly avoids crashing into the harbour wall. Finally, Derek revisits Usk, where he comes across something unexpected - an airfield, home of the South Wales Gliding Club, which has been in operation for 60 years. Derek joins them for a weather briefing before taking to the skies himself, where he witnesses amazing views of Usk and the Bristol Channel.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

programme.title: Honey

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Hamza Yassin heads to a secret location in Scotland’s Southern Uplands to join a dedicated team on an exciting mission to protect the fastest animal in the world - the peregrine falcon. Getting up close to three chicks, he discovers how DNA sampling is helping tackle the theft of these remarkable birds. Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: The results are in, and with a place in Blackpool at stake, the tension is high. Two couples will go head to head in the dance-off, but who will secure the final spot in the Tower Ballroom?

programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. A motorist races past traffic on an M53 slip road, while a bus squeezes past cyclists with barely room to spare, almost crushing them under the wheels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: The roadshow is at Roundhay Park in Leeds, where highlights include a rare Alfred Wallis painting, an unusual Fairyland Lustre bowl and an intriguing cap made from celebrated racehorse Red Rum’s hair. Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. Fiona Bruce explores the local history of high street chain Marks and Spencer when she sees some relics from the archives, while Joanna Hardy challenges her to spot the difference between a real diamond and a fake.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: The results are in, and with a place in Blackpool at stake, the tension is high. The pros take on one of the biggest trends in fiction as they bring the world of romantasy to life for their latest group performance, and fresh from his victorious stint on The Celebrity Traitors, Bash Croft performs in the ballroom. Two couples will go head to head in the dance-off, but who will secure the final spot in the Tower Ballroom?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: From winter storms to scorching summers, seasonal seas push animals to be resourceful, adaptable and adventurous. Those who can survive these dynamic seas reap rich rewards.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A rear-end shunt looks routine until a fraud investigator spots the occupants swapping seats. Could the dashcam have caught a crash-for-cash scam? In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. A motorist races past traffic on an M53 slip road, while a bus squeezes past cyclists with barely room to spare, almost crushing them under the wheels.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

In Leicestershire, cyclist Graham Cameron films two terrifying close calls on the same road. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In West Sussex, Natasha Raskin Sharp jets off to see a collection of memorabilia from an airline you might remember. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. With the hour ticking down, Wendy flummoxes her teammates with a piece of art glass in the form of a swan, and Vic and Tek get their own back on Thomas when he puts on a fashion show for them.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: A nightmare day for the team in the hub as three separate scams progress simultaneously. With so many plates to spin, the team split the work, dispatching both ground teams to separate addresses, whilst they themselves try to contact the other potential victim. With both ground teams on the road, it’s a race against the scammers tricking their victims into going down to the bank and withdrawing cash. But when one scam ends surprisingly, there is immediately another for the northern ground team to stop... two hours away from them!

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: Matt Allwright hears from Jane, who awoke in the middle of the night to discover two masked men breaking into her elderly parents' house. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan gives some top tips on what to do if you come home and find out you’ve been burgled. Matt also hears from Tami, whose doorbell captured the moment she took on a gang of wannabe bike thieves.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: After two decades down under, proud Yorkshireman Rich is heading back to his North Yorkshire roots with his Aussie wife, Jade, a grown-up daughter, two dogs and two cats in tow. With their £400,000 budget, Richie Anderson is tasked with finding this migrating menagerie a home from a selection which includes gorgeous cottages and an ecofriendly former head teacher’s house. And at a local farm shop, Richie discovers that serving up Yorkshire produce might be harder than it looks!

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: Will and Dom learn how a devastating fire put a 5,000-year-old craft in jeopardy. Meanwhile, Chris Shaw repairs a Gaelic pipe music book, and Dom has the chance to make his own sporran.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – George, Kelis, James, Stuart and Lucy – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: 1982, East Berlin. MI6 officer Martha Schmitt must maintain her humiliating cover identity as an ordinary East German woman having an affair with British diplomat Graham Anderson. She yearns for serious work, but when the chance to prove herself arrives, she botches it. To redeem herself, she is paired with Kurt Fischer, a CIA officer who ruined her mission. But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Having survived her close brush with Friedrich, Martha investigates Hermann’s murder with Kurt. A sceptical Friedrich orders his men, the inept Otto and Rolf, to also investigate it. After the Stasi seize Hermann’s notebook, Martha and Kurt must infiltrate his workplace, a strange sausage factory. They meet Kamilla, his sweet colleague – will she be the key to locating Greta? Meanwhile, now a fugitive, a terrified and confused Greta is running out of options for refuge. Where can she turn?

But the Stasi’s fearsome Friedrich Baumann has been observing Martha. When he makes a request of her, how can she refuse?

programme.title: Honey

Marc Allum is surprised to see Roger Moore modelling knitwear, while Clive Farahar compares a genuine first edition of Lady Chatterley’s Lover with a ‘pirated’ copy. Clive is also stunned to see a stark newspaper banner announcing the death of President John F Kennedy that had been used to line a drawer. Steven Moore is intrigued by a jug inscribed with the competitive victories of a famous brass band, and Alastair Dickenson is charmed by a Chinese silver bowl with a dragon design. At Crawley Museum, she reminisces about British Caledonian Airways – or BCal as it was affectionately known. Items include the tartan uniform worn by cabin crew and copies of the in-flight menu, grandly named la cuisine du ciel. At nearby Ardingly antiques fair, two teams of bargain hunters hope there’s no turbulence when they go shopping with experts Caroline Hawley and Thomas Forrester. With Caroline, it’s married couple Wendy and Phil, who don’t plan to 'dither', and with Thomas, it’s friends Vic and Tek, who reckon 'there’s no second place'. After 20 minutes, an exasperated Caroline urges her team to explore more than one stall; meanwhile, Thomas isn’t pulling any punches with his blues, rejecting a kitsch kitty biscuit barrel that Vic spots. programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: A knife attack in Inverness leads police to a volatile suspect and a house packed with blades, from Samurai swords to machetes and zombie knives. Released on bail while police await DNA results, he is soon wanted over another violent attack. On the Isle of Skye, rescuers race to find a climber who has been missing for three days in the mountains. And near Fort William, an American tourist has an unusual concern after a crash.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Deep in the Highlands, Loch Morar is home to a mysterious legend: Morag, a creature said to lurk beneath its dark, cold waters. Comedian and ecologist Zara Gladman teams up with parapsychologist Evelyn Hollow to investigate the sightings and meet locals whose accounts have kept the story alive for generations. A loch superintendent recalls a strange wake racing across the water, an angler describes three huge humps rising behind his boat, and a lifelong monster hunter reveals how easily shadows can fool even experts. As Zara gathers environmental DNA from the loch, could science finally offer an explanation? The results point to a familiar inhabitant: the European eel. But can it account for everything witnesses claim to have seen? With scepticism, humour and a healthy dose of curiosity, Zara and Evelyn dive into the mystery of Morag and ask whether this elusive monster is real, misunderstood or best left to legend.

programme.title: Mythland
programme.desc: Evelyn and Zara follow the trail of a local myth to uncover a moving story about industrial decline, community memory and the internet's power to reshape the past.

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Best-selling author and ex-gang member Graeme Armstrong travels to forgotten areas of Scotland to shine a light on the allure of gang life. He encounters drill music artists and street gang members, while also exploring his own past. Graeme tries to understand why young people are seduced by the perceived glamour and excitement of gang life by speaking to young people themselves.

programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Ex gang member and best-selling author Graeme Armstrong explores the underbelly of Dundee as he speaks to ex gang members in local schemes Whitfield and Kirkton and tries to understand the causes of recent civil unrest in the area. In this episode, Graeme focuses on what happens when the perceived glamour wears off and gang life begins to go wrong. programme.title: Street Gangs
programme.desc: Best-selling author and reformed gang member Graeme Armstrong explores how to escape the gang life. How do ‘young team’ members turn their lives around? Is it even possible? In this episode, Graeme explains that there were only ever three options he could see: death, prison or redemption. This time focusing on Glasgow, Graeme explores the Wyndford Scheme in Maryhill and travels to Glencoe to meet a man who, like himself, managed to turn his life around and leave gangs behind for good.

programme.title: Stevens & McCarthy
programme.desc: Stevens & McCarthy are back with their collection of comic characters, spoofs and musical comedy. At the roll van, Davie is not happy with the chat, a gamer mum loses her cool, and the girls think twinkly lights are the answer to all life's woes.

programme.title: Loop
programme.desc: Ex-Buzzcocks drummer John Maher shares punk memories and his current photography obsession, from his adopted home on the Isle of Harris. We hear how John toured the world supporting the Sex Pistols, and he opens up his scrapbooks to reveal meeting heroes such as Blondie’s Debbie Harry. Having lived a fast-paced life, John moved to Harris 20 years ago, and where he soon picked up his dusty camera and turned his lens to his adopted home. John aims to depict the island in a new way, with the focus not just on the breathtaking landscapes, but also the people and places left behind by humans. We join him as he completes his current project, which features a series of photographs focusing on a local family transforming an old croft into their perfect new home.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: New life is at the forefront of everyone’s mind, which means round-the-clock care for some. In Inverkip, after a successful pregnancy scan, Rachel and Camy are getting their sheds ready for the new crop of Park Cheviot Ewes – the best in their flock. They hope the ewes will give birth unaided, but they must stay vigilant in case they need to intervene. Nikki and Ollie welcome their first colony of rabbit kits as their breeding programme takes off. Things are looking up, but Ollie’s long hours at the maltings and the rise in cost of building materials mean their holiday pods are over budget and time. In the Cairngorms National Park, it’s out with the old and in with the new. Robert heads to market to sell previous year’s crop of spring calves – a nerve-wracking wait to find out what this year’s profit for a year’s hard work will be. Meanwhile, this year’s calves are due, so he’s up all hours ensuring each newborn is safely delivered.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Castlemilk housing estate on the southern edge of Glasgow, where he explores a local nature reserve that has transformed from perceived no-go zone to a thriving, green place. Arlene steps back in time in Aberdeenshire as she visits a rare shoemaker's workshop that shut up shop over 80 years ago. She meets the locals carefully conserving the shop’s contents. Anne is in the Black Isle, finding out about a charity funded by Children in Need that is providing bereavement support across the Highlands. And Dougie watches on as one couple’s herd of Aberdeen Angus cattle leaves the farm for good to go under the hammer at a dispersal sale.

programme.title: Our Lives
programme.desc: Quick hands, sharp instincts and a custom-built race car. Follow Scotland's first wheelchair-using racing driver as he prepares for his debut season.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: My Insta Scammer Friend
programme.desc: In this era of social media, we are given more access to the private lives of celebrities and influencers than ever before. But how well do we really know our favourite online friends? This film explores the murky and, at its worst, toxic, relationship between one influencer and her followers. The infamous viral scandals of pioneering internet sensation Caroline Calloway have captivated audiences across the globe, with some of her followers left feeling duped and scammed. But why did Caroline's actions garner so much attention? And what do influencers owe their followers who built the very foundations of their success?

What lies beyond the mists? Who or what are the Ux? The answers will lead the Doctor and her friends towards a deadly reckoning.

programme.title: Doctor Who (2005–2022)
programme.desc: As the new year begins, a terrifying evil from across the centuries of Earth's history is stirring. As the Doctor, Ryan, Graham and Yaz return home, will they be able to overcome the threat to planet Earth?

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda has decided to prove to herself and her friends that she can officially be an adult. She starts by looking after a toddler, but the soft play centre is too much of a lure and she gets stuck in a kids' tunnel. She then hosts a dinner party for eight, which ends in inevitable chaos.

programme.title: Miranda
programme.desc: Miranda has been caring for her ill mother for five very long days. Trapped in her flat and being barked at by Penny, she is forced to think about her life regrets. Before she has the chance to tick off her bucket list she gets ill, and Tilly, Gary and Stevie offer no sympathy or help at all.

programme.title: Gavin & Stacey
programme.desc: Comedy series about Essex boy Gavin and Welsh lass Stacey. After being phone buddies for months they finally arrange a rendezvous in Leicester Square, with Stacey's best friend Nessa and Gav's pal Smithy coming along for support.

programme.title: Gavin & Stacey
programme.desc: Comedy series about the long-distance relationship of Essex boy Gavin and Welsh lass Stacey. After a huge misunderstanding on the phone, Stacey thinks Gavin has finished with her. He drives to Wales to explain and ends up taking her home with him. Having never been further than Bridgend before, Stacey's trip to Essex is an eye-opening experience that ends with the biggest surprise of all.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: Josh Pugh hosts as Kate Sharp, Rachel Baker, Lucas Jones Ho, Patrick Conlan and Ravi Saini compete for a place in the grand final at Birmingham Town Hall in November.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s comedy talent search is back. More than a thousand comics applied, and just 30 made it through to the heats. This is the last of six, and five more acts are competing for the last place in this year’s grand final. The Box at Fargo Village, Coventry, will once again be converted into the BBC’s own New Comedy Club. Mancunian ray of sunshine Josh Jones is our host for the night. Joining him are the three judges – star of Ghosts and Taskmaster Kiell Smith-Bynoe, former NCA winner Dan Tiernan, and head judge, the multi-talented award-winning actor and comedian Amy Gledhill. Kwami Odoom, Stanley Magill, Harry Jenkins, Alasdair Wallace and Alana Jackson will each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final. Since the awards launched in 1995, past finalists and winners have included Peter Kay, Joe Lycett, Lee Mack, Julian Barratt, Josie Long, Shappi Khorsandi, Romesh Ranganathan, Alan Carr, Russell Howard, Lee Ridley, Tom Allen, Lauren Pattison and Sarah Millican.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: It's Aks's prom night, but will Mobeen let her go? With rumours about the debauchery at previous proms and the threat of a stabbing, Mobeen must safeguard her at any cost. Things get complicated when a classmate of Aks's, Ridwan, makes some very unwise decisions that leave Mobeen very concerned. Eight, meanwhile, is in danger of getting in too deep with a local wide boy, and he is potentially going to drag everyone down with him. Can Mobeen manage to keep everyone out of trouble?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: When Aks breaks her shoulder and heads for hospital with the boys, Accident and Emergency is the state of play. With Mobeen, Eight and Nate looking shifty de facto, the authorities start to get suspicious about how Aks may have sustained her injuries. In the waiting room, we see life in an overstretched A&E and the gang in a constant battle to prove their innocence, battle prejudice and, of course, keep Pakistani Rain Man (Eight) out of trouble.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: They say the past is never far away. And for Mobeen, it’s about to punch him in the throat. Cal, an old friend, makes an unexpected return to Small Heath, leaving Aks, Eight and Nate very concerned about what this means for Mobeen. Can he stay clear of trouble, or are things about to take a turn for the worse?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen
programme.desc: Dogs and ethnic minorities have a very bad track record. So when a clip involving Mobeen and an Alsatian goes viral, it’s a disaster. Aks is drawn in by the prospect of internet fame, while Mobeen tries to see if the spark between him and Aks’s teacher, Miss Aitken, is worth pursuing. The past finally catches up with our hero, though, leaving him with some very difficult decisions to make. Our season finale will change the game forever.

programme.title: The Golden Cobra
programme.desc: The Year 12 students get undermined when their fun school trip is switched at the last minute and they're forced to visit a mining museum, the Coal Hole. Mona is frustrated by Connor.

programme.title: The Golden Cobra
programme.desc: Miss Port invites all her posh friends to a dinner party to celebrate Jub's new job, as well as her new air fryer. Basil is finally caught by the TV licence men.

programme.title: The Golden Cobra
programme.desc: Rhys and his friends go to a college music gig after discovering that a girl in school might fancy him. But when he is threatened by Connor, they enlist local thug Malcolm to protect him.

programme.title: The Golden Cobra

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: Twenty-year-old Alexander McCartney, already known to police, is arrested and his devices seized after a 12-year-old girl in Scotland reports a serious catfishing abuse incident online. McCartney gives a ‘no comment’ interview while in custody, and without enough physical evidence to charge him, he is released on bail. Back home at his parents’ house, McCartney’s bail conditions are supposed to prevent him from using devices that can connect to the internet. Meanwhile, a second report comes in to the police about another catfishing abuse victim linked to online activity from McCartney’s home address. This time, it involves a young girl in New Zealand. As the police continue to gather up enough physical evidence to charge McCartney, the Cyber Crime Centre completes the analysis of one of his devices, revealing a prolific online predator at a scale never before seen by police in Northern Ireland.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: With hundreds of thousands of images of child abuse discovered on McCartney’s devices, the race is on to get him remanded into custody. McCartney is rearrested in the early hours of the morning, at which time police discover McCartney’s phone on his bedside table, where his final victim was abused on Snapchat just hours before. The US Department of Homeland Security notify the police in Northern Ireland of two more catfishing victims, this time in the United States, and a multiagency international investigation is triggered. As McCartney is remanded into custody, police across the world work together to identify and safeguard the thousands of victims discovered on McCartney’s devices. Police are especially keen to identify and locate a 14-year-old girl in Oregon, whose images McCartney used to catfish hundreds of other children. With McCartney due in court to plead guilty to charges of making indecent of images of children and blackmail, the case takes a different turn when Homeland Security finds an obituary page for Cimarron Thomas, one of his victims in West Virginia.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: As police piece together the last few minutes of Cimarron’s life, they realise McCartney was still online threatening her when she tragically shot herself. Police and prosecutors move quickly to establish if there’s a case for manslaughter. Police from Northern Ireland travel to West Virginia to conduct the manslaughter investigation, where they learn that Cimarron’s own family had no idea why she took her own life. In a tragic turn, they learn that 18 months after her death, Cimarron’s father had also died by suicide. In order to charge McCartney with manslaughter, the police have to prove that he foresaw the risk to her life. As they comb through the cyber evidence from his devices, they build a case for manslaughter and charge him. The case sets new legal precedent in the UK. More than five years after the police investigation began, McCartney is finally convicted and sentenced.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Dependent pest and stay-at-home-daughter Chi is once again forced to contend with life and death, and a long list of things she really ought to have done by now. Her dysfunctional family navigate the fallout of yet another unexpected bereavement, with mixed results. Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Karen has not only left the family in emotional turmoil but also serious debt. There’s no way Dave can keep up with the mortgage on his single wage, and he faces the very real threat of having to move in with Chi. Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: My Insta Scammer Friend
programme.desc: In this era of social media, we are given more access to the private lives of celebrities and influencers than ever before. But how well do we really know our favourite online friends? This film explores the murky and, at its worst, toxic, relationship between one influencer and her followers. The infamous viral scandals of pioneering internet sensation Caroline Calloway have captivated audiences across the globe, with some of her followers left feeling duped and scammed. But why did Caroline's actions garner so much attention? And what do influencers owe their followers who built the very foundations of their success?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC’s comedy talent search is back. More than a thousand comics applied, and just 30 made it through to the heats. This is the last of six, and five more acts are competing for the last place in this year’s grand final. The Box at Fargo Village, Coventry, will once again be converted into the BBC’s own New Comedy Club. Mancunian ray of sunshine Josh Jones is our host for the night. Joining him are the three judges – star of Ghosts and Taskmaster Kiell Smith-Bynoe, former NCA winner Dan Tiernan, and head judge, the multi-talented award-winning actor and comedian Amy Gledhill. Kwami Odoom, Stanley Magill, Harry Jenkins, Alasdair Wallace and Alana Jackson will each perform their set before the judges decide who will go through to the grand final. Since the awards launched in 1995, past finalists and winners have included Peter Kay, Joe Lycett, Lee Mack, Julian Barratt, Josie Long, Shappi Khorsandi, Romesh Ranganathan, Alan Carr, Russell Howard, Lee Ridley, Tom Allen, Lauren Pattison and Sarah Millican.

Eight, meanwhile, is in danger of getting in too deep with a local wide boy, and he is potentially going to drag everyone down with him. Can Mobeen manage to keep everyone out of trouble?

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

In the waiting room, we see life in an overstretched A&E and the gang in a constant battle to prove their innocence, battle prejudice and, of course, keep Pakistani Rain Man (Eight) out of trouble.

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

programme.title: Man Like Mobeen

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and asks if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. As the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: Piripenguins

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad and Cosima both think they're the best at pranking. Their prank war quickly spirals out of control, until Big Lizard finally reveals Proxima's real pranking champion!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's bathtime! The ducklings are determined Weasy will get clean.

But with Hoofius’s fear of gunk getting the better of him, evicting the slippery Smarg is not going to be easy.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons

programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Deadly 60
